questions.question: The value of (61+frac{2)/(5) times 75 div 6-(3 times 6 div (1)/(3)) times (1)/(6)}{5+(2)/(3) times(58-37)} is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The expression is:

(61 + (2/5) × 75 ÷ 6 - (3 × 6 ÷ (1/3)) × (1/6)) / (5 + (2/3) × (58 - 37))

**Formula used:**

Basic arithmetic operations: multiplication, division, and addition/subtraction.

**Calculation:**

Step 1: Simplify the numerator

(2/5) × 75 ÷ 6 = (150/5) ÷ 6 = 30 ÷ 6 = 5

(3 × 6 ÷ (1/3)) = (18 ÷ (1/3)) = 18 × 3 = 54

Now, (54 × 1/6) = 9

Substitute back into the expression:

Numerator = 61 + 5 - 9 = 57

Step 2: Simplify the denominator

(58 - 37) = 21

(2/3) × 21 = 14

Denominator = 5 + 14 = 19

Step 3: Final calculation

57 ÷ 19 = 3

**∴ The value of the expression is 3.**

questions.question: What is the value of ([(sin x+sin y)(sin y-sin x)])/([(cos x+cos y)(cos y-cos x)]) ?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Substitute **x = 0°** and **y = 90°** into the given expression.

⇒ Value = [(&sin; 0° + &sin; 90°)(&sin; 90° − &sin; 0°)] / [(&cos; 0° + &cos; 90°)(&cos; 90° − &cos; 0°)]

⇒ Value = [(0 + 1)(1 − 0)] / [(1 + 0)(0 − 1)]

⇒ Value = [1 × 1] / [1 × (−1)] = 1 / −1 = −1.

**∴ The correct answer is -1.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** [(&sin; x + &sin; y)(&sin; y − &sin; x)] / [(&cos; x + &cos; y)(&cos; y − &cos; x)]

**Formula used:** (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b² and &sin;² θ + &cos;² θ = 1.

⇒ Numerator = (&sin; y + &sin; x)(&sin; y − &sin; x) = &sin;² y − &sin;² x

⇒ Denominator = (&cos; y + &cos; x)(&cos; y − &cos; x) = &cos;² y − &cos;² x

⇒ Expression = (&sin;² y − &sin;² x) / (&cos;² y − &cos;² x)

⇒ Since &sin;² y = 1 − &cos;² y and &sin;² x = 1 − &cos;² x,

⇒ Numerator = (1 − &cos;² y) − (1 − &cos;² x) = &cos;² x − &cos;² y

⇒ Expression = (&cos;² x − &cos;² y) / (&cos;² y − &cos;² x) = −(&cos;² y − &cos;² x) / (&cos;² y − &cos;² x)

⇒ Expression = −1

**∴ The correct answer is -1.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Pythagorean Identity

For any angle θ, **sin² θ + cos² θ = 1**, which leads to 1 − sin² θ = cos² θ.

Difference of Squares

The algebraic identity **(a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²** is a fundamental tool for simplifying trigonometric products.

Sine Difference Identity

The expression **sin² A − sin² B** is equal to **sin(A + B) × sin(A − B)**.

Cosine Difference Identity

The expression **cos² B − cos² A** is also equal to **sin(A + B) × sin(A − B)**.</p

questions.question: The length of a side of an equilateral triangle is 18 cm. The area (in cm²) of the region lying between the circumcircle and the incircle of the triangle is [use pi=(22)/(7)]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The length of a side of an equilateral triangle is 18 cm.

**Formula used:**

Area of the region between circumcircle and incircle = π(R² - r²)

Where, R is the circumradius and r is the inradius.

For an equilateral triangle with side length a:

Circumradius, R = a/√3

Inradius, r = a/(2√3)

**Calculations:**

Side length a = 18 cm

R = 18/√3 = 18×√3/3 = 6√3 cm

r = 18/(2√3) = 18×√3/(2×3) = 3√3 cm

π = 22/7

Area = π(R² - r²)

⇒ Area = (22/7)×[(6√3)² - (3√3)²]

⇒ Area = (22/7)×[108 - 27]

⇒ Area = (22/7)×81

⇒ Area = 254(4)/(7) cm²

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: In a sweet, one-third is sugar. If the price of sugar now is (7)/(6) of the previous price, what is the effective percentage increase in the cost of the sweet?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

In a sweet, one-third is sugar.

The price of sugar now is dfrac{7}{6} of the previous price.

**Formula used:**

Effective percentage increase in cost = (New cost - Old cost) / Old cost × 100%

**Calculation:**

Let the original price of the sweet be 1 unit.

Cost of sugar in sweet = dfrac{1}{3} units

Cost of other ingredients = 1 - dfrac{1}{3} = dfrac{2}{3} units

New price of sugar = dfrac{7}{6} × dfrac{1}{3} = dfrac{7}{18} units

New cost of sweet = dfrac{7}{18} + dfrac{2}{3}

⇒ New cost of sweet = dfrac{7}{18} + dfrac{12}{18} = dfrac{19}{18} units

Effective percentage increase in cost = dfrac{dfrac{19}{18} - 1}{1} times 100

⇒ Effective percentage increase in cost = dfrac{1}{18} times 100

⇒ Effective percentage increase in cost = dfrac{100}{18}%

**∴ The correct answer is option (3) dfrac{100}{18}%.**

A dishonest dealer claims to sell his products at 24% loss on the cost price but uses 100 g weight instead of 200 g weight. His profit percentage is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net Multiplier = (Weight Ratio) × (Price Factor)

Weight Ratio = True weight / False weight = 200 / 100 = 2

Price Factor = (100 − 24) / 100 = 0.76

Net Multiplier = 2 × 0.76 = 1.52

Profit = 1.52 − 1 = 0.52

**∴ The correct option is B.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given:

⇒ Nominal weight = 200 g

⇒ Claimed loss = 24%

⇒ Actual weight used = 100 g

Formula Used:

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 ± Gain or Loss%)/100

Profit% = (SP − Effective CP) / Effective CP × 100

 
 Effective CP (100 units)
 
 Claimed SP (152 units)
 

 Profit = 52 units
 
• 
 Scale (g/units)

Calculations:

⇒ Let Cost Price (CP) of 1 g = 1 unit.

⇒ CP of 200 g = 200 units.

⇒ Dealer claims 24% loss, so SP = 200 × (100 − 24)/100 = 152 units.

⇒ Dealer delivers only 100 g, so Effective CP = 100 units.

⇒ Total Profit = SP − Effective CP = 152 − 100 = 52 units.

⇒ Profit percentage = (52 / 100) × 100 = 52%.

⇒ Profit in decimal form = 0.52.

**∴ The correct option is B.**

**__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Weight Formula

When a dealer sells at cost price but uses a false weight, Profit% = [ (Error) / (True Weight − Error) ] × 100.

Combined Profit with Weight and Price Change

Total Multiplier = (True Weight / False Weight) × (100 ± Profit or Loss%)/100. If result > 1, it is profit; if < 1, it is loss.

Marked Price and Dishonesty

If a dealer marks up by x% and uses a false weight, net gain = [ (100 + x) × (True weight / False weight) ] − 100.</p

questions.question: If x² - 6x - 1 = 0, then find the value of x²+(1)/(x²)-8.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

x²-6x-1=0, find x²+(1)/(x²)-8

Calculations:

x²-6x-1=0 ⇒ x²-6x-1= -6x

Divide by x: x-(1)/(x)=6

Identity: (x-(1)/(x))²=x²+(1)/(x²)-2

⇒ x-(1)/(x)=6

⇒ (x-(1)/(x))²=6²=36

⇒ x²+(1)/(x²)-2=36

⇒ x²+(1)/(x²)=38

⇒ x²+(1)/(x²)-8=30

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

A shopkeeper sold 3 wristwatches for ₹2,800 each. If he has sold the watches with 40%, 25% and 12% profit, respectively, then find his overall profit percentage (correct to 2 decimal places).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A shopkeeper sold 3 wristwatches for ₹2,800 each. If he has sold the watches with 40%, 25% and 12% profit, respectively, then find his overall profit percentage (correct to 2 decimal places).

**Formula used:**

Cost Price (CP) = dfrac{{Selling Price (SP)}}{1 + dfrac{{Profit Percentage}}{100}}

Overall Profit Percentage = dfrac{{Total Profit}}{{Total Cost Price}} times 100

**Calculation:**

SP₁ = ₹2800, Profit₁ = 40%

⇒ CP₁ = dfrac{2800}{1 + dfrac{40}{100}}

⇒ CP₁ = dfrac{2800}{1.4}

⇒ CP₁ = ₹2000

SP₂ = ₹2800, Profit₂ = 25%

⇒ CP₂ = dfrac{2800}{1 + dfrac{25}{100}}

⇒ CP₂ = dfrac{2800}{1.25}

⇒ CP₂ = ₹2240

SP₃ = ₹2800, Profit₃ = 12%

⇒ CP₃ = dfrac{2800}{1 + dfrac{12}{100}}

⇒ CP₃ = dfrac{2800}{1.12}

⇒ CP₃ = ₹2500

Total CP = CP₁ + CP₂ + CP₃

⇒ Total CP = 2000 + 2240 + 2500

⇒ Total CP = ₹6740

Total SP = 2800 + 2800 + 2800

⇒ Total SP = ₹8400

Total Profit = Total SP - Total CP

⇒ Total Profit = 8400 - 6740

⇒ Total Profit = ₹1660

Overall Profit Percentage = dfrac{1660}{6740} times 100

⇒ Overall Profit Percentage = dfrac{1660}{6740} times 100

⇒ Overall Profit Percentage = 24.63% or 0.2463

**∴ The correct answer is option 4.**

questions.question: Two trains, P and Q, are running on parallel tracks in opposite directions with lengths of 110 m and 140 m, respectively. Train P is running at a speed of 70 km/h and took 5 seconds to cross train Q. The speed of train Q is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of Train P = 110 m

Length of Train Q = 140 m

Speed of Train P = 70 km/h

Time taken to cross = 5 seconds

**Formula used:**

Relative Speed = (Length of Train P + Length of Train Q) / Time

Relative Speed = Speed of Train P + Speed of Train Q (since they are moving in opposite directions)

**Calculations:**

Relative Speed = (110 + 140) m / 5 s

⇒ Relative Speed = 250 m / 5 s

⇒ Relative Speed = 50 m/s

Convert Speed of Train P to m/s:

Speed of Train P = 70 km/h

⇒ Speed of Train P = 70 × (1000 m / 3600 s)

⇒ Speed of Train P = 70000 m / 3600 s

⇒ Speed of Train P = 19.44 m/s

Relative Speed = Speed of Train P + Speed of Train Q

50 m/s = 19.44 m/s + Speed of Train Q

⇒ Speed of Train Q = 50 m/s - 19.44 m/s

⇒ Speed of Train Q = 30.56 m/s

Convert Speed of Train Q to km/h:

Speed of Train Q = 30.56 m/s

⇒ Speed of Train Q = 30.56 × (3600 s / 1000 m)

⇒ Speed of Train Q = 110 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: The value of (17)/(sec ² theta)+10 sin ² theta+(7)/(1+cot ² theta) is:
questions.solution:

(17 / sec²θ) + 10sin²θ + (7 / (1 + cot²θ))

**Calculation:**

Step 1: Simplify each term

We know that 1 / sec²θ = cos²θ and 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ. So, we can rewrite the expression as:

17cos²θ + 10sin²θ + 7sin²θ

Step 2: Combine like terms

10sin²θ + 7sin²θ = 17sin²θ

Now, the expression is:

17cos²θ + 17sin²θ

Step 3: Apply the identity sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

⇒ 17(sin²θ + cos²θ) = 17 × 1 = 17

**∴ The value of the expression is 17.**

questions.question: A shopkeeper offers a 10% discount on dairy products and still manages to make a 20% profit. What is the actual cost (in Rs.) to the shopkeeper of a dairy product marked Rs. 420?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹420

Discount = 10%

Profit = 20%

**Formula used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) - Discount

Cost Price (CP) = Selling Price (SP) / (1 + Profit%)

**Calculation:**

Discount Amount = 10% of 420

⇒ Discount Amount = 0.10 × 420 = ₹42

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) - Discount Amount

⇒ SP = 420 - 42 = ₹378

Cost Price (CP) = SP / (1 + Profit%)

⇒ CP = 378 / (1 + 0.20)

⇒ CP = 378 / 1.20

⇒ CP = ₹315

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: If a=(sqrt{2}-1)⁽¹⁾/⁽³⁾, then the value of (a-(1)/(a))³+3(a-(1)/(a)) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Recognize the algebraic identity: **(x − 1/x)³ + 3(x − 1/x) = x³ − 1/x³**.

Given **a = (√2 − 1)¹/³**, cubing both sides gives **a³ = √2 − 1**.

The reciprocal **1/a³ = 1/(√2 − 1)** rationalizes to **√2 + 1**.

The required value is **a³ − 1/a³ = (√2 − 1) − (√2 + 1) = −2**.

**∴ The correct answer is -2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **a = (√2 − 1)¹/³**

**Formula Used:** **(x − y)³ = x³ − y³ − 3xy(x − y)**

⇒ **a = (√2 − 1)¹/³**

⇒ Cubing both sides: **a³ = √2 − 1**

⇒ Let the expression be **E = (a − 1/a)³ + 3(a − 1/a)**

⇒ Using the expansion of **(a − 1/a)³**: **E = [a³ − 1/a³ − 3(a)(1/a)(a − 1/a)] + 3(a − 1/a)**

⇒ **E = a³ − 1/a³ − 3(a − 1/a) + 3(a − 1/a)**

⇒ **E = a³ − 1/a³**

⇒ Rationalize **1/a³**: **1/(√2 − 1) × (√2 + 1)/(√2 + 1) = (√2 + 1) / (2 − 1) = √2 + 1**

⇒ **E = (√2 − 1) − (√2 + 1) = √2 − 1 − √2 − 1 = −2**

**∴ The correct answer is -2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity

The cubic expansion **(x − y)³ = x³ − y³ − 3xy(x − y)** is often rearranged to solve for **x³ − y³**.

Rationalization

To simplify **1/(√x − √y)**, multiply by the conjugate **(√x + √y)** to utilize the difference of squares: **a² − b²**.

Reciprocal Property

If **x = √n − √(n − 1)**, then its reciprocal is always **1/x = √n + √(n − 1)** because the product **(√n − √(n − 1))(√n + √(n − 1)) = 1**.</p

questions.question: A seller marks an item for Rs. 500 and sells it at a discount of 25%. He also gives a gift worth Rs. 65. If he still makes 24% profit, then the cost price of the item (in Rs.) is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked price = Rs. 500

Discount = 25%

Gift worth = Rs. 65

Profit = 24%

**Formula used:**

1. Selling price after discount = Marked price × (1 - Discount%)

2. Cost price = (Selling price - Gift) / (1 + Profit%)

**Calculation:**

Step 1: Calculate the selling price after a 25% discount.

⇒ Selling price = 500 × (1 - 0.25)

⇒ Selling price = 500 × 0.75 = Rs. 375

Step 2: Subtract the value of the gift from the selling price to get the effective selling price.

⇒ Effective selling price = 375 - 65 = Rs. 310

Step 3: Calculate the cost price using the profit formula.

⇒ Cost price = 310 / (1 + 0.24)

⇒ Cost price = 310 / 1.24 = Rs. 250

**∴ The cost price of the item is Rs. 250.**

questions.question: In an election, 95% of the total voters cast their votes. In this election, there were only two candidates A and B. The winner A, by obtaining 75% of the total votes, defeated his contestant B by 5500 votes. Find the total number of voters in the election.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

In an election, 95% of the total voters cast their votes.

Winner A obtained 75% of the total votes.

A defeated B by 5500 votes.

**Formula used:**

Total Votes Cast = Total Voters × 0.95

Votes for A = Total Voters × 0.75

Votes for B = Total Votes Cast - Votes for A

Difference in Votes = Votes for A - Votes for B

**Calculations:**

Let Total Voters = x

Total Votes Cast = x × 0.95

Votes for A = x × 0.75

Votes for B = Total Votes Cast - Votes for A

⇒ Votes for B = x × 0.95 - x × 0.75

⇒ Votes for B = x × (0.95 - 0.75)

⇒ Votes for B = x × 0.20

Difference in Votes = Votes for A - Votes for B

⇒ 5500 = x × 0.75 - x × 0.20

⇒ 5500 = x × (0.75 - 0.20)

⇒ 5500 = x × 0.55

⇒ x = 5500 / 0.55

⇒ x = 10000

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: A man borrowed Rs. 29,000 for 3 years and Rs. 45,000 for 5 years at the same rate of simple interest. If he paid a total interest of Rs. 62,400, then what was the rate of interest?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal₁ (P₁) = ₹29,000

Time₁ (t₁) = 3 years

Principal₂ (P₂) = ₹45,000

Time₂ (t₂) = 5 years

Total Interest (I) = ₹62,400

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = P × r × t / 100

Total Interest = SI₁ + SI₂

Where, r = rate of interest

**Calculation:**

SI₁ = P₁ × r × t₁ / 100

SI₂ = P₂ × r × t₂ / 100

Total Interest = SI₁ + SI₂

62,400 = (29,000 × r × 3 / 100) + (45,000 × r × 5 / 100)

⇒ 62,400 = (87,000r / 100) + (225,000r / 100)

⇒ 62,400 = (87,000r + 225,000r) / 100

⇒ 62,400 = 312,000r / 100

⇒ 62,400 = 3,120r

⇒ r = 62,400 / 3,120

⇒ r = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**
